q: When must a tax invoice be issued for goods involving movement?
options: Before or at the time of removal of goods
At the end of the month
exp: For supplies without movement, it's before or at the time of delivery.

q: What's the time limit for a normal service provider to issue a tax invoice?
options: Within 30 days from the date of supply
exp: Banks, insurance companies and NBFCs get 45 days.

q: What's the maximum length of an invoice serial number?
options: 16 characters, unique for the financial year
exp: It can contain letters, digits, hyphen and slash.

q: Which of these is NOT a mandatory field on a tax invoice under rule 46?
options: Place of supply with state name for inter-state supplies
exp: Recipient's GSTIN is needed for registered buyers, but not PAN.

q: For a B2C invoice of ₹60,000 to an unregistered buyer, what recipient details must appear?
options: Name and address of the recipient, delivery address, and state name and code
exp: For unregistered recipients, these are required when the invoice value is ₹50,000 or more.

q: How many copies of an invoice are needed for goods?
options: Triplicate: original for recipient, duplicate for transporter, triplicate for supplier
exp: Services need duplicate. E-invoices reduce the reliance on physical copies.

q: A retailer sells many items under ₹200 each to walk-in unregistered customers who don't ask for invoices. What can it do?
options: Issue one consolidated invoice at the end of each day
exp: Proviso to rule 46.

q: A business can have separate invoice series for different branches in the same state under one GSTIN.
exp: Multiple series are fine as long as each number is unique within the financial year. All series are reported in GSTR-1 Table 13.

q: An export invoice without IGST must carry which endorsement?
options: 'Supply meant for export under bond or letter of undertaking without payment of integrated tax'
exp: With IGST paid, the endorsement is 'supply meant for export on payment of integrated tax'.

q: A composition taxpayer or a supplier of exempt goods issues a:
exp: Bill of supply has no tax charged.

q: When a supplier receives an advance, what document does it issue?
exp: If the supply is later cancelled and no invoice issued, it issues a refund voucher.

q: Which situation calls for a delivery challan instead of a tax invoice?
options: Goods sent to a job worker
exp: Other cases: liquid gas where quantity isn't known, transport not constituting a supply, and SKD/CKD goods in lots.

q: A business that has just received its registration certificate can issue revised invoices for supplies made between the effective date and the grant date within:
options: One month from the date of issue of the registration certificate
exp: Section 31(3)(a).

q: A registered person buys from an unregistered supplier under RCM. What does it issue?
options: A self-invoice (and a payment voucher when paying)
exp: Section 31(3)(f), now required within 30 days under rule 47A.

q: When does a supplier issue a credit note?
options: When the invoice value was too low
When the taxable value or tax charged exceeds what's payable, goods are returned, or services are deficient
exp: A debit note is for when the value or tax charged was lower than what's payable.

q: What's the last date to declare a credit note for an FY 2024-25 supply?
options: 30 November 2025, or the annual return date, whichever is earlier
exp: After that date, the supplier can't reduce its output tax through the credit note, though a commercial credit note is still possible.

q: One credit note can be issued against multiple invoices.
exp: The 2018 amendment allowed a credit note for 'one or more tax invoices'.

q: A supplier issues a credit note reducing tax. What must the recipient do?
options: Reduce its ITC by the corresponding amount
exp: The supplier's reduction in output tax is allowed only if the recipient reduces its ITC. With IMS, the recipient's accept or reject action on credit notes now flows through directly.

q: Is there a time limit for issuing a debit note?
options: No time limit for issuing it, though ITC on it is subject to section 16(4)
exp: Debit notes increase liability, so the law doesn't cap when they can be issued.

q: Where are credit and debit notes issued to registered persons reported in GSTR-1?
exp: CDNR for registered, CDNUR for unregistered recipients.

q: A customer returns goods worth ₹1,00,000 + ₹18,000 IGST in December 2025, from a sale made in June 2024. Can the supplier reduce its tax through a GST credit note?
model: The credit note is for a supply of FY 2024-25. The time limit for declaring it is 30 November 2025 (or the annual return date if earlier). December 2025 is past that, so the supplier can't reduce its output tax. It can issue a financial credit note without GST, and bear the ₹18,000 as a cost or settle it commercially. The recipient keeps its ITC.
points: Credit note linked to FY of original supply
Past the deadline, no GST reduction
exp: The software should warn when a user tries to raise a GST credit note against an invoice from a closed period.

q: A tax invoice can be issued by a registered person who is:
options: Any registered person making a taxable supply (other than composition taxpayers, who issue bills of supply)
exp: Composition taxpayers issue bills of supply.

q: A signature or digital signature on a tax invoice:
options: Is required, but invoices issued through e-invoicing with the IRP's digital signature don't need a separate signature
exp: Rule 46(q), with the e-invoice exception.

q: For goods sent on approval (sale or return), when must the invoice be issued?
options: When it becomes known the supply has occurred, or 6 months from removal, whichever is earlier
exp: Section 31(7).

q: A client's invoice number format is 'MUM/2025-26/INV/000123' (22 characters). What's the issue?
options: Invoice numbers are limited to 16 characters, so the IRP or portal will reject it
exp: Common fix: drop the redundant 'INV' and shorten the year, e.g. 'MUM/2526/000123'.

q: A client gives a customer a 2% cash discount for early payment, not agreed on the original invoice. How should it be documented?
options: A financial credit note without GST, since it doesn't meet the section 15(3) conditions
exp: GST stays as originally charged, and the customer keeps its ITC.
